newsitem.title: USA: SKW Metals guilty of ferro-silicon price fixing.
newsitem.headline: SKW Metals guilty of ferro-silicon price fixing.

text.p: SKW Metals and Alloys, the U.S. subsidiary of Germany's VIAG AG, and SKW Metals' executive vice-president Charles Zak, were both found guilty of violating the Sherman anti-trust act by fixing ferro-silicon prices, a court official said.

SKW Metals and Zak had denied fixing ferro-silicon and silicon metal prices in a case brought to the U.S. District Court, Western District of New York in Buffalo, following a Grand Jury probe led by the U.S. Justice Department.
A court official said SKW Metals and Zak were found not guilty of fixing silicon metal prices, the second charge of violating the Sherman Act they faced.
Sentencing will be sometime in July, the court official added.
SKW Metals officials were not available for immediate comment.

The charge SKW Metals and Zak were found guilty of stated that beginning at least as early as late 1989 and continuing at least until mid-1991, the defendants and others engaged in a combination and conspiracy to fix prices of commodity ferro-silicon products in the United States.
Elkem Metals, part of Norway's Elkem A/S, and American Alloys had already agreed to pay fines in out-of-court settlements after pleading guilty to the Sherman Act violations.
Elkem paid a $1 million fine, and several current and past Elkem employees testified on behalf of the government during the trial in Buffalo.
The Sherman Act charges stem from former SKW Metals' President Greg Magness' decision to tell U.S. Justice about alleged price fixing in the U.S. silicon metal and ferro-silicon markets.
Magness was granted immunity from prosecution after blowing the whistle.
Industry sources said the U.S. government offered an out-of-court settlement to SKW Metals and Zak on several occasions but were rebuffed.
Globe Metallurgical and AIMCOR, two other U.S. silicon producers, were not indicted despite being included in the Justice probe.
Ferro-silicon is used by steelmakers and foundries.

Class action suits have already been filed by some foundries, and leading steelmakers seeking damages from price fixing. The lawsuits name combinations of SKW Metals, Elkem, American Alloys and AIMCOR.
In a further twist to the price-fixing case, Brazil's two biggest ferro-silicon producers have been mulling whether to ask the International Trade Commision to reopen a ferro-silicon dumping case.

A lawyer on behalf of the Brazilians has said that the period of investigation in the dumping suit brought by the U.S. Ferroalloys Association against Brazilian ferro-silicon imports overlapped with the price-fixing period for which SKW Metals and Zak were found guilty.
